summary: Preinstall script harvests npm tokens from installer's Desktop and exfiltrates to remote webhook
details: Package advertises itself as a trivial 'add two numbers' utility but its preinstall lifecycle script enumerates files under the installer's Desktop directory, reads the first.txt file, applies a regex matching npm authentication tokens (npm_[A-Za-z0-9_-]+), and transmits any match via HTTPS GET to a hardcoded third-party webhook at webhooktest.net (path 019fb2f4-bacc-70d0-bc69-04f805508e0d). The stated arithmetic purpose is inconsistent with reading installer-owned filesystem content or contacting an external host. Installer npm tokens grant publish rights over the installer's own packages, enabling downstream supply-chain compromise.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
